General-purpose technologies are those that reshape entire economies and societies. Energy was one. Artificial intelligence may be another. Today, their paths are converging. AI depends on reliable, affordable energy to operate at scale, while energy systems increasingly leverage AI to plan networks, manage demand, strengthen cybersecurity, and improve service delivery.
 
When integrated well, AI can reinforce the digital energy stack. It can improve energy data quality, support smarter grid planning, reduce losses, and expand access through better customer engagement and financing models. But this potential is not automatic. Without deliberate investment and governance, AI risks deepening existing divides, especially where data gaps, weak infrastructure, and limited institutional capacity persist.
 
Countries are responding to these emerging challenges - and opportunities. Including through:
 
🤖 Using AI to accelerate energy outcomes, including project financing and inclusive access models
🏛️ Building AI skills across government, especially in procurement and public service delivery
🌱 Positioning Green AI as a development advantage by aligning AI growth with renewable energy foundations
 
AI’s impact will not be defined by algorithms alone. It will be shaped by how well energy systems, institutions, and governance evolve together as part of the digital energy stack.
